From 306039414932c80f8420695a24d4fe10c84ccfb2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:08:02 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] apparmor: fix: limit the number of levels of policy
 namespaces

Currently the number of policy namespaces is not bounded relying on
the user namespace limit. However policy namespaces aren't strictly
tied to user namespaces and it is possible to create them and nest
them arbitrarily deep which can be used to exhaust system resource.

Hard cap policy namespaces to the same depth as user namespaces.

Fixes: c88d4c7b049e8 ("AppArmor: core policy routines")
Reported-by: Qualys Security Advisory <qsa@qualys.com>
Reviewed-by: Ryan Lee <ryan.lee@canonical.com>
Reviewed-by: Cengiz Can <cengiz.can@canonical.com>
Signed-off-by: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>

diff --git a/security/apparmor/policy_ns.c b/security/apparmor/policy_ns.c
index 01b653a3609b..5a907a875d8f 100644
--- a/security/apparmor/policy_ns.c
+++ b/security/apparmor/policy_ns.c
@@ -223,6 +223,8 @@ static struct aa_ns *__aa_create_ns(struct aa_ns *parent, const char *name,
 	AA_BUG(!name);
 	AA_BUG(!mutex_is_locked(&parent->lock));
 
+	if (parent->level > MAX_NS_DEPTH)
+		return ERR_PTR(-ENOSPC);
 	ns = alloc_ns(parent->base.hname, name);
 	if (!ns)
 		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/security/apparmor/include/policy_ns.h b/security/apparmor/include/policy_ns.h
index d646070fd966..cc6e84151812 100644
--- a/security/apparmor/include/policy_ns.h
+++ b/security/apparmor/include/policy_ns.h
@@ -18,6 +18,8 @@
 #include "label.h"
 #include "policy.h"
 
+/* Match max depth of user namespaces */
+#define MAX_NS_DEPTH 32
 
 /* struct aa_ns_acct - accounting of profiles in namespace
  * @max_size: maximum space allowed for all profiles in namespace

## Summary of Modifications

The patch introduces a hard limit on the nesting depth of AppArmor policy namespaces to prevent resource exhaustion from arbitrarily deep namespace creation.

### Changes in Each File

1. **`security/apparmor/include/policy_ns.h`**  
   - Added a new macro `MAX_NS_DEPTH` with value `32`, matching the maximum depth of user namespaces in the kernel.

2. **`security/apparmor/policy_ns.c`**  
   - In function `__aa_create_ns()`, added a guard check: if the parent namespace’s `level` already exceeds `MAX_NS_DEPTH`, the function returns an error pointer (`-ENOSPC`) instead of proceeding to allocate a new namespace.

### Relationship Between the Changes

The macro `MAX_NS_DEPTH` defined in the header file is used as the upper bound in the namespace creation function. This single–point definition ensures consistency and allows the enforcement of the nesting limit. The check in `__aa_create_ns()` prevents any namespace from being created at a depth greater than 32, effectively capping the total nesting of policy namespaces and mitigating resource exhaustion attacks.

2.34.1

The patch addresses a resource exhaustion vulnerability in AppArmor by limiting the nesting depth of policy namespaces. It introduces a constant `MAX_NS_DEPTH` (set to 32, matching the user namespace limit) and adds a check in the namespace creation function to reject creation when the parent namespace already exceeds this depth.

**Modifications in each file:**
- **`security/apparmor/include/policy_ns.h`**: Added a new macro `#define MAX_NS_DEPTH 32` to define the maximum allowed depth for namespace nesting.
- **`security/apparmor/policy_ns.c`**: In `__aa_create_ns()`, added a guard clause that returns `ERR_PTR(-ENOSPC)` if `parent->level` is greater than `MAX_NS_DEPTH`, preventing further allocation.

**Relationship between the modifications:**  
The constant defined in the header provides the limit value used in the runtime check within the source file. The check ensures that no new namespace is created beyond the defined depth, thereby enforcing the resource cap.

## Summary of Modifications

The patch introduces a hard limit on the nesting depth of AppArmor policy namespaces to prevent resource exhaustion from arbitrarily deep namespace hierarchies.

### Modifications per File

- **`security/apparmor/include/policy_ns.h`**  
  Added a new macro constant `MAX_NS_DEPTH` with value `32`, matching the maximum depth allowed for user namespaces.

- **`security/apparmor/policy_ns.c`**

### Relationship of the Changes

The macro `MAX_NS_DEPTH` defined in the header provides the constant value that the implementation file uses to enforce the depth limit. Together, they ensure that no policy namespace can be created at a depth greater than 32, thereby capping the nesting chain and mitigating the risk of exhausting system resources via deep namespace recursion.
